````text
# #4185: Patch: audio volume sliders announce percentages to screen readers and disable when all sound is muted
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When a player using a screen reader opens the sound settings, the volume sliders now read out as percentages rather than bare numbers. For example, moving the music slider announces '80 percent' instead of just '80'. In addition, when all sound is muted, the individual volume sliders appear dimmed and cannot be adjusted until sound is turned back on. Players notice immediately that the sliders are inactive instead of wondering why adjusting them makes no sound.

## Why

- In `apps/web/src/audio/AudioControls.tsx`, volume sliders (`<input type="range">`) render an adjacent visual readout `<output className="audio-controls__value" htmlFor={inputId} aria-hidden="true">{value}%</output>`. Because the readout is explicitly marked `aria-hidden="true"` and the range input lacks `aria-valuetext`, screen readers announce only the raw integer value (e.g. '80') rather than the unit percentage ('80%'). In contrast, `SpeedSlider` in `apps/web/src/settings/controls.tsx` provides `aria-valuetext={speedLabel(props.speed)}`.
- When `settings.muted` is true (toggled either by the 'Mute all sound' checkbox or the board HUD audio toggle), the five volume sliders (`audio-master`, `audio-sfx`, `audio-crowd`, `audio-voice`, `audio-music`) remain visually active and draggable. However, adjusting them produces no preview sounds (the audio engine drops all play requests while muted) and changes levels that have no audible effect.
- Disabling the sliders when `settings.muted` is true gives clear visual and assistive-technology feedback that the sliders are inactive while mute is active.

## Proposal

1. In `apps/web/src/audio/AudioControls.tsx`:
   - Add `aria-valuetext={`${value}%`}` to the volume `<input type="range">` elements.
   - Add `disabled={settings.muted}` to each volume range input.
   - Add disabled styling or a modifier class in `apps/web/src/audio/audio.css` for disabled volume rows and range inputs (`opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed;`).
2. In `apps/web/src/audio/AudioControls.test.tsx`:
   - Add unit tests verifying that all five volume sliders expose `aria-valuetext` matching their percentage values (e.g. `'80%'`).
   - Add unit tests verifying that muting disables all five volume sliders, and unmuting re-enables them.

## Where it lands

- Files:
  - `apps/web/src/audio/AudioControls.tsx` (add `aria-valuetext` and `disabled={settings.muted}`)
  - `apps/web/src/audio/audio.css` (styling for disabled volume rows and range inputs)
  - `apps/web/src/audio/AudioControls.test.tsx` (tests for `aria-valuetext` and disabled state)
- SPEC sections:
  - SPEC §10.11 ("Settings")
  - `docs/polish/2-sound.md` (B30, B54)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each volume range input (`audio-master`, `audio-sfx`, `audio-crowd`, `audio-voice`, `audio-music`) has `aria-valuetext` set to `${value}%` (e.g., `'80%'`).
- [ ] When `settings.muted` is true, all five volume sliders have `disabled` set to true.
- [ ] When `settings.muted` is false, all five volume sliders have `disabled` set to false.
- [ ] Disabled volume sliders and their rows reflect the inactive state visually in `audio.css`.
- [ ] Existing audio controls tests in `apps/web/src/audio/AudioControls.test.tsx` pass without regressions, and new assertions prove the percentage announcements and mute disabled state.

## Size and risks

- Size: small (`difficulty:medium`). 3 files touched (`AudioControls.tsx`, `audio.css`, `AudioControls.test.tsx`), approximately 20-30 lines of code and tests.
- Risks: minimal. Does not touch engine, cards, networking, or audio playback logic; purely accessibility and interaction feedback in the web client settings UI.

When a screen-reader user moves a sound volume slider, it announces the value as a percentage (e.g. `80%`), and while `Mute all sound` is on, all five volume sliders are disabled and visibly dimmed so it is clear they do nothing until sound returns. This touches only `AudioControls` presentation: no engine, card, audio-playback, or settings-store behavior changes.

## Files to touch

| Path | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/audio/AudioControls.tsx` | change | In the `VOLUMES.map` range `<input>`, add `aria-valuetext` and `disabled`; nothing else |
| `apps/web/src/audio/audio.css` | change | Add disabled styling for volume rows and range inputs at the end, near `.audio-controls__row input[type="range"]` |
| `apps/web/src/audio/AudioControls.test.tsx` | change | Add tests for `aria-valuetext` percentages and mute/unmute disabled state |

Do not touch: `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `crates/engine`, `crates/cards`, `crates/ai`, `crates/server`, the audio engine/playback (`engine.ts`, `director.ts`, `cues.ts`), the settings store (`settings.ts`), or any other web file. Governing spec: SPEC §10.11 ("Settings", `spec/10-engine-guide.md` "Settings" paragraph: volumes, mute, voice on/off) and `docs/polish/2-sound.md` B30, B54. No new ruling note: percentage announcements and disabling sliders while muted are pure UI feedback, not an undecided rules question, so no `spec/rulings/R*.md`, no `spec/pending/` paragraph, and no `r<n>`/`R<n>` test name is required.

## Steps

1. `apps/web/src/audio/AudioControls.tsx`, in `AudioControls`'s `VOLUMES.map` volume `<input type="range">` (the block starting `<input id={inputId} type="range"`): add exactly two props, copying the `SpeedSlider` pattern in `apps/web/src/settings/controls.tsx` (which sets `aria-valuetext={speedLabel(props.speed)}`):
   - `aria-valuetext={\`${value}%\`}` (`` value `` is the already-computed `percent(settings, key)` in scope, so the default master slider exposes `'80%'`).
   - `disabled={settings.muted}` (reads the same `settings` object the mute checkbox already reads; no new state, no new import).
   - Leave the adjacent `<output ... aria-hidden="true">{value}%</output>` exactly as is; it stays the sighted readout while `aria-valuetext` becomes the announced value.
2. `apps/web/src/audio/audio.css`, immediately after the existing `.audio-controls__row input[type="range"]` rule: add exactly:
   ```css
   .audio-controls__row input[type="range"]:disabled {
     opacity: 0.5;
     cursor: not-allowed;
   }
   .audio-controls__row:has(input[type="range"]:disabled) {
     opacity: 0.5;
   }
   ```
   - Do not rename or restyle any existing rule; do not add a modifier class in the `.tsx` (the `:has` selector dims the whole row, label and readout included, from the `disabled` attribute alone).
3. `apps/web/src/audio/AudioControls.test.tsx`, append one new `describe` block (after the `B54` block, before the `R631` block), following the file's existing `screen.getByTestId` style:
   - `it("announces each volume slider as a percentage")`: render `<AudioControls />` with default settings, then for each of `audio-master`, `audio-sfx`, `audio-crowd`, `audio-voice`, `audio-music`, assert `slider.getAttribute("aria-valuetext")` equals `` `${slider.value}%` `` (e.g. master `'80%'`); then `writeAudioSettings({ master: 0.25 })` (or `fireEvent.change` on `audio-master` to `"25"`) and assert that slider's `aria-valuetext` is `'25%'`.
   - `it("disables all five volume sliders while muted, and re-enables on unmute")`: render `<AudioControls />`, assert all five sliders have `disabled === false`; set mute via `fireEvent.click(screen.getByTestId("audio-mute"))` and assert all five have `disabled === true`; click the mute checkbox again and assert all five have `disabled === false`. Prefer clicking the real checkbox over calling `writeAudioSettings` directly so the test proves the UI path.

## Tests

- `apps/web/src/audio/AudioControls.test.tsx`:
  - `announces each volume slider as a percentage` — asserts each of the five `data-testid` sliders exposes `aria-valuetext` equal to its displayed percent, and that changing a value updates it (fails without Step 1's `aria-valuetext`).
  - `disables all five volume sliders while muted, and re-enables on unmute` — asserts `disabled` is false by default, true for all five after muting, false again after unmuting (fails without Step 1's `disabled`).
- Commands:
  - `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/audio/AudioControls.test.tsx`
  - `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`

## Done when

- [ ] Each volume range input (`audio-master`, `audio-sfx`, `audio-crowd`, `audio-voice`, `audio-music`) exposes `aria-valuetext` of `${value}%`.
- [ ] With `settings.muted` true, all five sliders have `disabled === true`; with false, all five have `disabled === false`.
- [ ] Disabled sliders and their rows render dimmed/inactive via `audio.css` (`opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed;` or equivalent).
- [ ] New assertions above pass and the pre-existing `AudioControls.test.tsx` tests still pass: `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/audio/AudioControls.test.tsx` green, plus `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` green.

## Risks

- CSS `:has` support: all supported browsers for the app implement it; if a reviewer objects, the fallback is a conditional row class in the `.tsx` — do not preemptively add both.
- `disabled` inputs do not fire `onChange`, so no preview-tick logic changes; the engine's muted acceptance gate is untouched, so playback behavior cannot change.
- No hidden-information or replay risk: the change reads only the local audio settings store and adds ARIA/styling attributes.

## Open questions

None.

## Goal

When a screen-reader user moves a sound volume slider, it announces the value as a percentage (e.g. `80%`), and while `Mute all sound` is on, all five volume sliders are disabled and visibly dimmed so it is clear they do nothing until sound returns. This touches only `AudioControls` presentation: no engine, card, audio-playback, or settings-store behavior changes.

## Files to touch

| Path | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/audio/AudioControls.tsx` | change | In the `VOLUMES.map` range `<input>`, add `aria-valuetext` and `disabled`; nothing else |
| `apps/web/src/audio/audio.css` | change | Add disabled styling for volume rows and range inputs at the end, near `.audio-controls__row input[type="range"]` |
| `apps/web/src/audio/AudioControls.test.tsx` | change | Add tests for `aria-valuetext` percentages and mute/unmute disabled state |

Do not touch: `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `crates/engine`, `crates/cards`, `crates/ai`, `crates/server`, the audio engine/playback (`engine.ts`, `director.ts`, `cues.ts`), the settings store (`settings.ts`), or any other web file. Governing spec: SPEC §10.11 ("Settings", `spec/10-engine-guide.md` "Settings" paragraph: volumes, mute, voice on/off) and `docs/polish/2-sound.md` B30, B54. No new ruling note: percentage announcements and disabling sliders while muted are pure UI feedback, not an undecided rules question, so no `spec/rulings/R*.md`, no `spec/pending/` paragraph, and no `r<n>`/`R<n>` test name is required.

## Steps

1. `apps/web/src/audio/AudioControls.tsx`, in `AudioControls`'s `VOLUMES.map` volume `<input type="range">` (the block starting `<input id={inputId} type="range"`): add exactly two props, copying the `SpeedSlider` pattern in `apps/web/src/settings/controls.tsx` (which sets `aria-valuetext={speedLabel(props.speed)}`):
   - `aria-valuetext={\`${value}%\`}` (`` value `` is the already-computed `percent(settings, key)` in scope, so the default master slider exposes `'80%'`).
   - `disabled={settings.muted}` (reads the same `settings` object the mute checkbox already reads; no new state, no new import).
   - Leave the adjacent `<output ... aria-hidden="true">{value}%</output>` exactly as is; it stays the sighted readout while `aria-valuetext` becomes the announced value.
2. `apps/web/src/audio/audio.css`, immediately after the existing `.audio-controls__row input[type="range"]` rule: add exactly:
   ```css
   .audio-controls__row input[type="range"]:disabled {
     opacity: 0.5;
     cursor: not-allowed;
   }
   .audio-controls__row:has(input[type="range"]:disabled) {
     opacity: 0.5;
   }
   ```
   - Do not rename or restyle any existing rule; do not add a modifier class in the `.tsx` (the `:has` selector dims the whole row, label and readout included, from the `disabled` attribute alone).
3. `apps/web/src/audio/AudioControls.test.tsx`, append one new `describe` block (after the `B54` block, before the `R631` block), following the file's existing `screen.getByTestId` style:
   - `it("announces each volume slider as a percentage")`: render `<AudioControls />` with default settings, then for each of `audio-master`, `audio-sfx`, `audio-crowd`, `audio-voice`, `audio-music`, assert `slider.getAttribute("aria-valuetext")` equals `` `${slider.value}%` `` (e.g. master `'80%'`); then `writeAudioSettings({ master: 0.25 })` (or `fireEvent.change` on `audio-master` to `"25"`) and assert that slider's `aria-valuetext` is `'25%'`.
   - `it("disables all five volume sliders while muted, and re-enables on unmute")`: render `<AudioControls />`, assert all five sliders have `disabled === false`; set mute via `fireEvent.click(screen.getByTestId("audio-mute"))` and assert all five have `disabled === true`; click the mute checkbox again and assert all five have `disabled === false`. Prefer clicking the real checkbox over calling `writeAudioSettings` directly so the test proves the UI path.

## Tests

- `apps/web/src/audio/AudioControls.test.tsx`:
  - `announces each volume slider as a percentage` — asserts each of the five `data-testid` sliders exposes `aria-valuetext` equal to its displayed percent, and that changing a value updates it (fails without Step 1's `aria-valuetext`).
  - `disables all five volume sliders while muted, and re-enables on unmute` — asserts `disabled` is false by default, true for all five after muting, false again after unmuting (fails without Step 1's `disabled`).
- Commands:
  - `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/audio/AudioControls.test.tsx`
  - `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`

## Done when

- [ ] Each volume range input (`audio-master`, `audio-sfx`, `audio-crowd`, `audio-voice`, `audio-music`) exposes `aria-valuetext` of `${value}%`.
- [ ] With `settings.muted` true, all five sliders have `disabled === true`; with false, all five have `disabled === false`.
- [ ] Disabled sliders and their rows render dimmed/inactive via `audio.css` (`opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed;` or equivalent).
- [ ] New assertions above pass and the pre-existing `AudioControls.test.tsx` tests still pass: `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/audio/AudioControls.test.tsx` green, plus `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` green.

## Risks

- CSS `:has` support: all supported browsers for the app implement it; if a reviewer objects, the fallback is a conditional row class in the `.tsx` — do not preemptively add both.
- `disabled` inputs do not fire `onChange`, so no preview-tick logic changes; the engine's muted acceptance gate is untouched, so playback behavior cannot change.
- No hidden-information or replay risk: the change reads only the local audio settings store and adds ARIA/styling attributes.

## Open questions

None.

## State
- Built per plan: `aria-valuetext` + `disabled={settings.muted}` on all five volume sliders, `:disabled`/`:has` dimming in `audio.css`, two new tests in `AudioControls.test.tsx`. No departures from the plan except the percentage test drives the change through `fireEvent.change` (direct `writeAudioSettings` outside `act()` did not re-render synchronously).
- Done; verified: `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/audio/AudioControls.test.tsx` 9/9 green, `typecheck` green (needed `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=6144` — default heap OOMs in this environment), eslint clean on both touched `.tsx` files.

## Log
- 2026-11-18: added the two props to `AudioControls.tsx` and the disabled CSS; added the new `describe` block to the test file.
- 2026-11-18: test run 8/9 — the direct-store write did not re-render; switched to `fireEvent.change`, re-ran 9/9 green, typecheck (large heap) and eslint green.
